text:
maria: Heads-up — we merged the dependency update for libserial (CVE-2028-284) earlier today. Patch landed in main at 14:02 UTC. We need a quick validation plan before we promote to prod: smoke tests, perf regression check, and verify audit trail/KMS behaviour for rotation paths.

samir: Do we have the CVSS/exploitability details? Want to confirm priority and whether to emergency rollback if we see regressions.

maria: CVSS 7.5, remote info leak w/ crafted payloads; exploit code not public yet. Patch recommended, prioritized P1 for next deploy window. No rollback planned unless errors spike.

kate: For audit logs — after the lib change, will user+key metadata still be emitted for KMS decrypt calls? Need to make sure our audittrail shows key_id and caller identity for compliance.

lucas: I ran the staging smoke earlier. Saw KMS decrypt calls still include key_id but user field was intermittently missing. Grabbed snippet from staging logs:

```
2028-09-12T14:10:23Z INFO kms.decrypt key_id=projects/prod/keys/rdw-key-42 caller=svc-ingest
2028-09-12T14:10:24Z INFO kms.decrypt key_id=projects/prod/keys/rdw-key-42 caller=
```

lucas: Not sure yet if it's the libserial change or unrelated log parser.

maria: Good catch. Can someone run the k8s canary with verbose logging on the KMS client and enable auditlog sampling to 100% for 15m? We need to confirm whether missing caller is coming upstream.

samir: I can schedule a canary in the eu-west-1 pool at 15:00 UTC. Plan: 5% traffic for 10 minutes, run perf harness (qps=200, p95 latency baseline) and run a synthetic that triggers decrypts. If any of these fail we halt.

ops-bot: CI pipeline: libserial-update -> canary image built (sha: b7f3a2d). Integration tests: 112/118 passed, 6 flaky tests flagged.

maria: Which tests flaked? Are any related to KMS or RBAC?

ops-bot: Flaky tests: token-cache-expiry, ingress-auth-tls, session-replay-3 (maybe unrelated). KMS integration tests passed.

kate: Even if KMS tests passed, we still need to confirm auditlog completeness. Samir, when you run the canary, capture:
- auditlog entries for decrypts (fields: timestamp, key_id, principal)
- p95/p99 latency vs baseline
- error rate and 5xx counts

samir: Will do. Also will enable fallback routing to smaller model variant in the canary policy to reduce blast radius.

lucas: If we see missing caller fields, I'll run a targeted build that reverts the logging parser change and compare logs side-by-side.

maria: OK schedule looks good. If canary metrics are green after 10m we promote to 50% for another 20m and then full. If errors or latency regressions >10% at p95 we rollback instantly.

deploy-bot: Canary started in eu-west-1 at 15:00 UTC (image b7f3a2d). Monitoring: perf-harness running (qps=200).

samir: Canary first 3m: p95 +2.3% vs baseline, error rate 0.02% (ok), auditlog sampling shows 100 decrypt events, 2 missing principal fields. Capturing log slices and uploading to /tmp/canary-logs-1842008888.tar.gz

maria: Two missing fields is concerning. Lucas please diff parser. Kate: can you confirm whether this still meets compliance thresholds or do we need a hold?

kate: For audit compliance we need caller present in >99.9% of decrypts. 2/100 is 98% — fail. Hold promotion and investigate.

lucas: I'll spin a debug build that pins the previous log normalization and run a quick smoke on a small subset. ETA 30m.

maria: Thanks all — holding. Keep updates in this thread. If anyone finds a quick mitigation (log enrichment via sidecar), propose it here. :eyes:
